rulers.name: Alfred Meyer-Waldeck
rulers.title: Governor and commander of the garrison
rulers.note: Siege page: the garrison was 'commanded by naval Captain and Governor Alfred Meyer-Waldeck' (3,625 men); the page gives no appointment year.

correction.text: the leasehold of Jiaozhou Bay round Qingdao, 552 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row (the Empire of Japan dossier removed four Tsingtao cells from its 1915 shape; here they are the German leasehold). The page: 'Covering an area of 552 km2 (213 sq mi)', 'centered on Jiaozhou Bay ... on the southeastern coast of the Shandong Peninsula', plus 'a 50 km wide neutral zone' in which China gave up sovereign rights. A radius of 18 km round Qingdao (2 cells, 506 km2 on the grid, ratio 0.92) stands for the leasehold; the neutral zone is not drawn.

region.text: Jiaozhou Bay and Qingdao, leased to Germany

ledger.note: 6 March 1898: 'on 6 March 1898, the German Empire retreated from outright cession of the area and accepted a leasehold of the bay for 99 years, or until 1997'; the Reichstag ratified on 8 April 1898 and Kiautschou was placed under imperial protection on 27 April (page). The seizure was earlier: 'At 06:00, Sunday, 14 November 1897, Cormoran steamed into the inner harbor'.

7 November 1914: 'On 7 November 1914, the bay was occupied by Japanese forces'; the Siege of Tsingtao page: the fortress 'surrendered to the Japanese forces' on 7 November, after a siege 'between 27 August and 7 November 1914', and 'The Allies took formal possession of the colony on 16 November 1914'. Japan returned it to China on 10 December 1922 (Kiautschou page), outside this state's life.

wars.name: Siege of Tsingtao
wars.outcome: Japanese victory: the fortress surrendered on 7 November 1914 after a siege from 27 August; the garrison of 3,625 under Governor Meyer-Waldeck was taken.
wars.note: The Kiautschou page dates Japan's ultimatum to 15 August 1914 and declaration of war to 23 August 1914.

certainty.note: Fixed by the 1898 lease, but no page gives the line; the 18 km radius is a stand-in within 10 percent of the page's 552 km2. The neutral zone is not drawn.

sources.title: Kiautschou Bay concession

sources.title: Siege of Tsingtao
sources.note: 27 August - 7 November 1914; garrison; formal possession 16 November 1914.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from two pages. Not settled: (1) the page's 50 km neutral zone is not drawn (the page gives no boundary); (2) Cliopatria folds four Tsingtao cells into Japan's shapes until the jk-01-d repair removed them; the colony overlaps nothing now; (3) the dossier ends at the Japanese occupation (7 November 1914), not the 1922 return, since the leasehold ended then; the Japanese-held Tsingtao is the Empire of Japan dossier's occupation event; (4) the Kiautschou page says Japan occupied the area again 1937-1945, which is outside this dossier. Counterpart qing-dynasty (ea-08-a/b) and german-empire (not mine) are cited as slugs.
